name: DentalPULSE
product: The DentalPULSE Pod: an ultrasonic cleaner for dentures, night guards, retainers and aligners. Advertise ONLY the Pod (user rule Oct 13: no Travel Pod concepts; no Pod Max; no standalone tablet boxes). Exception: offer-based creatives for the Ultimate Cleaning Bundle show its contents as sold (Pod + Travel Pod + 30-tablet box), and Pod Denture Bundle offers show the Pod with its free gifts.
audience: Adults who wear a removable oral appliance (clear aligners/Invisalign, retainers incl. permanent/wire, dentures, night/mouth guards, sleep apnea devices), plus parents of teens with retainers and adult children buying for a parent with dentures. Men and women.
palette: clean bright white and soft pale blue backgrounds, DentalPULSE blue (#1E73E8) for headlines and pills, dark navy (#0B1F3A) body text, occasional black premium backgrounds
font_style: clean modern sans-serif (like Inter/SF Pro), bold headlines, generous white space, clinical-but-friendly
prompt_rules: The product MUST be the exact DentalPULSE device in the attached reference photo, unchanged. The Pod: a smooth matte-white rounded dome with fine vertical ribbing all around the body, a thin horizontal seam near the base, a slightly domed top cap with the 'DentalPULSE' wordmark (black, 'Dental' regular + 'PULSE' bold); when open, a round white hinged lid flips up from the back (the inside of the lid has four small square light points) over a brushed stainless-steel cleaning basin. Keep proportions and every detail; only change angle, lighting and setting. Do not invent buttons, screens, displays, colors or logos. Show no other DentalPULSE products (no Pod Max, no Travel Pod, no tablet boxes) unless the reference photo is a bundle, in which case show exactly the bundle's items at their true relative sizes.

Oral appliances (clear aligners, retainers, dentures, night guards) must look anatomically correct and realistic: clear aligners are thin transparent trays shaped like a full upper or lower arch; dentures have realistic pink gums and natural teeth. No distorted mouths or teeth on people.
Render every word of on-image text exactly as written in quotes, spelled correctly, and no other text.
High-end e-commerce photography quality, sharp focus, natural soft shadows, no watermarks, no extra logos.
The cleaning cycle is always 5 minutes: any timer, clock or copy shows 5 minutes (05:00), never 3 minutes.
claims_to_avoid: shipping speed or free shipping/returns beyond the 120-day guarantee (not confirmed)
invented counts: customers, units sold, reviews, 'X,000 dentists'; press logos or other awards
a strike-through 'was' price other than the store's compare-at prices ($180 Pod Denture Bundle, $300 Ultimate Cleaning Bundle)
naming or showing logos of competitor ultrasonic pods (Zima, Sonic Dental, GuruNanda, oPro, Novapod): show them unbranded
medical treatment claims (cures infections, prevents disease)

denture_wearer.name: Denture/partial wearer, 60+, cleans with Polident tablets + brush
denture_wearer.source: ~55% of survey; every current winner (comparison/listicle/native ads) targets dentures; pains: adhesive/Fixodent goo, yellowing, food in crevices, slimy feel, smell

denture_caregiver.name: Adult child or spouse buying for a parent/partner with dentures
denture_caregiver.source: 'Who noticed': husband/wife/grandchildren; gift buyers in survey; denture wearers 60+ often gifted tech

night_guard.name: Teeth grinder (TMJ/bruxism), 30–60, night guard turned yellow and cloudy
night_guard.source: ~22% of survey; 'gross yellow and cloudy', 'never felt clean', soap/toothpaste routine; negatives: old yellow stains don't fully reverse

retainer.name: Retainer wearer (adult post-ortho) or parent of a teen with retainers
retainer.source: ~13% of survey; 'clear again, not milky', tablets made retainer brittle, buildup in crevices; 'daughter got one for her retainer'

aligner.name: Clear aligner/Invisalign wearer, 25–45, on the go
aligner.source: ~6% of survey but high-value category; 'white film', 'trays look cloudy', 'no more smell'; Zima/oPro/Novapod compete hardest here

switcher.name: Burned buyer who already tried a cheap Amazon/Zima/GuruNanda pod
switcher.source: ~15% of survey previously owned another pod; 'failure of 2 others', 'three previous buys and none worked'; matches winning 'tested 7 pods' comparison angle

format_guides.fb_comment: Render the testimonial as a real Facebook mobile comment thread, pixel-faithful to the current Facebook app: light grey rounded comment bubble on white, small round profile photo on the left (realistic person matching the persona), commenter name in bold dark text (first name + last initial), comment text in Facebook's system sans font at normal comment size, a grey row under the bubble reading like "2d   Like   Reply", and a small overlapping reaction pill (like/love icons + a count) at the bubble's lower right. Optionally 2–3 stacked comments with replies indented. Plain, native, not designed; no Facebook logo.
format_guides.trustpilot: Render the testimonial as a real Trustpilot review card, faithful to Trustpilot's current design: white card with thin light-grey border, reviewer row with a small round initials avatar, reviewer first name + last initial and country code, a row of five green square star tiles with white stars (Trustpilot green #00B67A), a short bold review title, the review text in a clean sans font, and a small grey date. Show individual review cards only: no Trustpilot logo, no TrustScore, no overall rating or review count, no 'Verified' badge.
format_guides.x_post: Render as a real X (formerly Twitter) post screenshot, faithful to the current X app in light mode: white background, round profile photo top-left, display name in bold black, then grey @handle and "· 3h", the post text in X's Chirp-like sans at native size (black, left-aligned, no quotation marks), optionally an attached photo with rounded corners, then a grey engagement row with the reply, repost, like and view icons and small counts, all in X's thin grey icon style. No blue verification checkmark, no X logo, no 'Twitter' bird. It must read as a genuine X post, not a designed graphic.
format_guides.cartoon_3d: Render as a still frame from a modern 3D animated feature film: soft global illumination, rounded appealing character designs with expressive eyes, rich but tasteful color, cinematic depth of field, subsurface skin shading. Characters look stylized-cute, not realistic.
format_guides.comic_strip: Render as a modern webcomic strip: 3 or 4 panels with thin black borders and white gutters, clean confident ink outlines, flat colors with light shading, round speech bubbles containing exactly the quoted lines, simple expressive characters. Panel order reads left to right, top to bottom.
format_guides.flat_illustration: Render as a modern flat vector editorial illustration: simple geometric characters with minimal facial features, a limited 4–5 color palette from the brand colors, soft subtle grain texture, generous negative space, clean sans-serif type.
format_guides.claymation: Render as a stop-motion claymation still: characters and props sculpted from plasticine with visible fingerprint texture and slightly imperfect edges, handmade miniature set, warm soft studio lighting, shallow depth of field.
format_guides.retro_cartoon: Render as a 1930s rubber-hose cartoon still: black-and-white or sepia ink with one accent color, bendy limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, wobbly hand-inked lines, vintage film grain and vignette, old-timey title card lettering.
format_guides.anime_soft: Render as a frame from a soft hand-painted anime film: lush painterly backgrounds, gentle watercolor light, clean line art for characters, warm nostalgic mood.

format_guides_note: Testimonial/review ads use fb_comment or trustpilot; tweet-style ads use x_post. Cartoon/animation formats (user rule, Oct 11: use them, both brands): cartoon_3d, comic_strip, flat_illustration, claymation, retro_cartoon, anime_soft. Aim for ~15–20% of every batch.

methods: Polident tablets (overnight soak, blue water, minty smell, film stays)
old_methods.show: Real-looking Polident and Efferdent boxes/tablets are fine as the old method we replace; never imply they endorse us.

ultimate_cleaning_bundle.best_for: aligners, retainers, night guards (home + on the go)

naming_rule: Call it an "ultrasonic cleaner" (e.g. "the DentalPULSE ultrasonic cleaner", "this $99 ultrasonic cleaner") in most headlines, especially top-of-funnel for unaware audiences who don't know what a 'Pod' is. Use "the Pod" only as a secondary/brand reference or in offer/retargeting copy.
copy_rules: Direct response, aggressive, specific. Lead with the pain in the customer's words, agitate, then the mechanism, then proof/offer. Short punchy lines, numbers, imperatives.

Controversial is welcome (user Oct 13): attack Polident/Efferdent tablets ('pool chemicals and bleach', 'Do not place in mouth — read that again'), brushing/soap/vinegar/bleach, 'big pharma kept this from you', cheap pods that 'look like they work'. Use verbatim hooks from research/notion_brief.md §2 and §8 and feedback_deep_dive.md §9.

Make BACTERIA and YELLOW STAINS explicit in the creative (they are the #1 and #2 purchase reasons in the feedback sheet: 68% and 40%). Visualize them: biofilm close-ups, petri dishes, brown/murky water after a cycle, yellow vs white.

Dentures: push yellow → white hard ('white as the day I got them' is a real result). Night guards/retainers/aligners: frame yellow/cloudy/milky as bacteria + film ('that yellow is bacteria', 'stops it turning yellow', 'clear again', 'no white film') — do NOT promise years of set-in yellow vanish in one cycle (night-guard yellow-stain buyers were the least satisfied).
Show the invisible: brown water, debris lifting, cavitation bubbles — several unhappy buyers saw 'no vibrations, just noise'.
Funnel mix every batch: ~65% top-of-funnel (problem/enemy/mechanism/controversy, no price) and ~35% offer-based (40% OFF $99.95 + gifts + 120-day guarantee; bundles).
